title: `ttlMs` / `cacheScope`
description: Freshness and sharing hints required on cacheable results, giving a time to live in milliseconds and a public or private scope.
question: Does the framework respect the server's caching hints?
why: New in 2026-07-28, and it cuts both ways. A framework that ignores `ttlMs` re-fetches constantly or serves stale results; one that ignores `cacheScope` risks caching a private, authorization-scoped result and serving it to another caller.
usage_note: Not published. Candidate source: count of public MCP servers using this capability. Not estimated, so the panel stays empty until the corpus is scanned.

notes.openai-agents: OpenAI Agents SDK 0.23.1: `MCPServerStdio` passes `cache=None` to the mcp client, which switches off its ttl-aware cache, and `cache_tools_list` defaults to off. Every list goes back to the server inside `ttlMs`. Turning `cache_tools_list` on caches until `invalidate_tools_cache()`, which ignores `ttlMs` too.
notes.pydantic-ai: Pydantic AI 2.54.0: `MCPToolset` caches the tool list (`cache_tools`, on by default) until a `list_changed` notification or until the toolset closes. It ignores `ttlMs`, so a re-list after the hint expired is served stale.
notes.strands: Strands Agents 1.59.0: `list_tools_sync` asks the server on every call, inside the `ttlMs` window as well as after it, so the hint is neither honored nor needed. `load_tools`, which an agent reads, keeps the first listing until an `on_tools_changed` refresh and does not read `ttlMs` either.
notes.vercel_ai: Vercel AI SDK (@ai-sdk/mcp 2.0.73): `client.tools()` calls `tools/list` every time and ignores `ttlMs`. A re-list inside the ttl goes to the server, and so does one after it, so it is never stale but never cached.
notes.openai_agents_js: OpenAI Agents SDK (JS) 0.20.0: the server's `ttlMs` is not honoured on the path the SDK uses. `listTools` passes `cacheMode: 'bypass'` to the MCP client on a 2026-07-28 session, so every re-list inside the TTL went to the server. The SDK's own `cacheToolsList` option is a separate, TTL-blind cache.
notes.agno: Agno 3.1.2: `build_tools` asks the server on every call, inside the `ttlMs` window as well as after it, so the hint is not read; an `Agent` without `refresh_connection=True` keeps the first listing regardless.
notes.copilot_sdk: GitHub Copilot SDK 1.0.19 (Copilot runtime 1.0.95): `session.rpc.mcp.listTools` ignores `ttlMs`. The re-list inside the 1500 ms window went to the server, as did the one after it.
notes.langchain4j: LangChain4j 1.22.0-beta32: `DefaultMcpClient` caches `tools/list` and refreshes the cache only on `notifications/tools/list_changed`. It ignores `ttlMs`, so a re-list after the TTL is still served from the stale cache.
notes.ms_agent_framework_dotnet: Microsoft Agent Framework (.NET) 1.24.0 (ModelContextProtocol 2.2.0): `McpClient.ListToolsAsync` ignores `ttlMs`. The re-list inside the 1500 ms window went to the server, as did the one after it.
